summary: GKE Workload Identity Pool mapping mismatch breaking autoscaler credentials for dedicated clusters
description:
Issue summary: During recent onboarding of a new dedicated GKE cluster (cluster-id: ded-gke-3-us-east1) the cluster-autoscaler is failing to authenticate with GCP due to an incorrect Workload Identity Pool -> Service Account mapping. This prevents node pool scale-ups for some ML training jobs and is causing elevated pod Pending counts on customer Dedicated workloads.

Impact: Autoscaler cannot obtain credentials to create / attach node VMs for certain autoscale events. Affected hosted Dedicated environments are intermittently unable to scale GPUs which increases tail latency for jobs and blocks scheduled batch workloads. No user data exfiltration suspected.

Observed behaviour: Autoscaler logs show token exchange failures with 403 "requester project does not own mapping" followed by repeated scale attempts and eventual timeout. The provisioner marks the node-pool request as failed and leaves pods in Pending.

Expected behaviour: Workload Identity mapping should allow the kube-controller-manager/component acting as the autoscaler to exchange a Workload Identity token and impersonate the dedicated-provisioner service account to create nodes.

Additional context: This cluster was migrated from a staging project using an infra-as-code change and a small variation in the workload identity pool provider name (dash vs underscore) appears to be the root cause. The problem only affects clusters created after 2026-03-09 and only for projects using the ded-gke-3 nodepool naming scheme.
environment: prod | gcp | us-east1 | cluster: ded-gke-3-us-east1 | dedicated-provisioner
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated GKE cluster using infra template v3.7 with workload identity provider name formatted with an underscore (e.g. projects/123/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/ded_pool_01/providers/provider_a)
2) Deploy standard dedicated-provisioner and autoscaler helm charts with service account annotations to use workload identity
3) Trigger an autoscale by scheduling a GPU-heavy training job that increases pending pod count > node-pool capacity
4) Observe autoscaler logs in stackdriver: token exchange attempts and 403 errors referencing mapping ownership
5) Confirm that a cluster created from template v3.6 (provider name with dash) does not reproduce the failure
logs: 2026-03-11T14:02:18Z autoscaler: failed to exchange token: 403 requester project does not own mapping (projects/123/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/ded-pool-01/providers/provider-a)
2026-03-11T14:03:02Z provisioner: nodepool create request failed: unauthorized to impersonate serviceAccount: dedicated-provisioner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: provider name mismatch introduced by IaC template normalization (underscore vs dash) caused Workload Identity mapping to be scoped to a different pool id.
gcloud command used: gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers describe provider-a --project=redwood-prod --location=global --workload-identity-pool=ded-pool-01

Confirmed IAM binding exists between dedicated-provisioner service account and provider on older clusters; absent on affected clusters (compare 'gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding' output).
Patched a staging cluster by adding explicit iamcredentials binding and autoscaler began successfully creating nodes (temporary proof-of-concept).

Risk: Fix requires either corrective IaC change reverting provider name or a targeted migration script updating existing pool/provider identifiers; must coordinate with infra and security for permissions to alter workload identity pool providers in production.
comments: 2026-03-11 15:10 - Rohit Patel: Assigned for triage. I'll validate IaC templates and see if the migration produced drift in provider identifiers.

2026-03-11 16:45 - SRE Oncall (Maya Chen): Confirmed the same 403 error on ded-gke-3 cluster in us-east1; linked stackdriver traces in notes. We can temporarily add iam binding for dedicated-provisioner but need approval from infra-security.

2026-03-12 09:20 - Infra (Liam O'Connor): Looks like terraform module 'gke_workload_identity' defaults changed between versions; we can either roll module back or run a one-off reconcile script. Security wants least-privileged changes only.
2026-03-12 12:30 - Rohit Patel: Created a reconciliation PR to normalize provider names and added migration runbook. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/1894
next_steps: 1) Approve temporary IAM binding for dedicated-provisioner to get immediate scaling restoration (infra-security approval required). 2) Merge PR to normalize IaC provider naming and run migration script across affected projects. 3) Add post-deploy validation to CI to detect provider-name drift. 4) Close ticket once autoscaler behavior verified on 3 consecutive scale events.
workaround: Temporarily add IAM policy binding allowing dedicated-provisioner to impersonate service account on affected projects: gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding dedicated-provisioner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --member=\"serviceAccount:service-@pool-provider\" --role=\"roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser\" (requires infra-security approval).
